{"id":"mimid-1wgh.140.3","title":"WHOWAS: which MIMI user a nick used to mean","description":"WHOWAS (314 RPL_WHOWASUSER, 369 RPL_ENDOFWHOWAS, 406 ERR_WASNOSUCHNICK), the thinnest of the verbs that still has something true to say.

WHY IT IS THIN: a nick here is derived from a MIMI user, so it does not churn the way a nick on a network does. There is no nick history in the sense RFC 2812 means.

WHY IT IS NOT EMPTY: the derivation is not injective. A nick is held (crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/names.rs, `Held`), collisions take a suffix, and a user's display name can change, so the same nick can have meant different MIMI users at different times, and the same user can have appeared under different nicks. That is exactly the question WHOWAS is for, and it is a question with a security edge: a user who remembers talking to a nick deserves to know which user URI it was, because a nick that has been reused is how a person is impersonated in a client's scrollback.

WHAT IT SHOULD ANSWER: for a nick this connection has seen, the MIMI user URI it mapped to and when, bounded by what the front end actually retains. For anything else, 406 ERR_WASNOSUCHNICK, which is the correct refusal and a better answer than 421.

DECIDE AND RECORD, since this is where it could go wrong: whether the mapping is kept per connection or in the store. Per connection is cheap, truthful and forgets on reconnect; in the store it outlives a client and becomes a record of who the user talked to, which is a new thing to protect and to expire. Per connection is the smaller claim and the suggested one, with the limitation written down rather than implied.

NEVER answer for a nick belonging to another provider's user in a way that asserts anything the authenticated MIMI sender did not say: the sender is always the authenticated MLS sender, and a nick mapping is a rendering, not an identity claim.

{"design":"IMPLEMENTED. `WHOWAS <nick> [<count>]` answers, for a nick this run of the
daemon has given, which MIMI user URI it stands for and since when: 314
RPL_WHOWASUSER then 312 RPL_WHOISSERVER then 369 RPL_ENDOFWHOWAS, or 406
ERR_WASNOSUCHNICK then 369, or a single 431 ERR_NONICKNAMEGIVEN with no nick.
Class 1 of epic mimid-1wgh.140. No credential is checked and no boundary is
added: command.rs is reached only after registration.

WHY IT HAS SOMETHING TO SAY. Not because a display name can change: a nick is
built from the user URI alone (`base_identity`), never from a display name. The
derivation is non-injective through collision — two URIs with the same local
part and the same first DNS label want the same nick, and the second is
suffixed — so which user holds the bare nick depends on arrival order, and that
order can differ between runs, because `Names::load` gives a kept
`ext["irc"]["nick"]` again when it is malformed or was taken first. Within one
run nothing is ever unbound, so the mapping is immutable and WHOWAS reports it
with a "since".

WHERE THE TIMES LIVE (the bead's open question): in `Names`, as `when:
BTreeMap<folded nick, ms>`, written in `take_nick`, the one function through
which every nick passes. Not per connection (every IRC connection here is the
same user, and `user_of` already resolves every nick the run gave, so WHOIS and
ISON answer for all of them; a per-connection copy would need a call at roughly
ten rendering sites) and not in the store (a durable record of whom the user
talked to, deferred to mimid-1wgh.140.8). Not a second structure with an
eviction bound either: `Session::who` admits any `mimi://` URI the client
types, so WHOIS mints nicks from the socket with no flood control, and a
bounded mirror would have let a client push the user's own nick out and get 406
where WHOIS still answers. The readings are decision mimid-1wgh.143.

`<count>` is accepted and not read: at most one entry exists per nick, so the
reply is one entry or none, which satisfies a positive count (at least one) and
"a full search" (Modern; RFC 2812 §3.6.3 for non-positive) alike. One nick is
read, Modern's `<nick>` and not RFC 2812's comma list, so `WHOWAS a,b` is 406;
no TARGMAX token, which would promise a list mimid never reads.

312's `<server info>` stays a server description, `mimid-agent`, with "this run
has had this nick since <ISO-8601>" in the same parameter: a bare timestamp
would give one numeric two meanings inside command.rs, where WHOIS 312 already
sends `mimid-agent`, and would read as when the user was first met.

ALSO FIXED HERE, because 314 cannot be written without it: `base_identity` now
passes the URI's domain through `host_part`, mapping every character outside
`[A-Za-z0-9.-]` to `_`. Modern says 311's `<host>`, whose argument meanings 314
takes, cannot start with a `:`, and a space in it would split the parameter
after it; `parse_user_uri` constrains the domain's characters not at all, and
`WHOIS mimi://:1/u/bob` from the client's own line was enough to emit a
malformed 311.

TESTS. names.rs: the fields, the own nick, ASCII-only folding, the service nick
and a URI and a comma list all unknown, the time bounded by `now_ms` around the
call; the collision case, where the nick must name its holder and not the user
who was displaced; the hostile authority. command.rs (a new test module):
`whowas_lines` byte for byte against Modern's Reply Examples, the nick read
from the first parameter and not the last, and 369 closing both outcomes.
tests/irc.rs: the whole exchange over a registered connection, which answered
421 before the verb existed.
"}

WHOWAS answers 314, 312 and 369 for a nick this run gave, 406 then 369 otherwise, and a single 431 with no nick; the times live in Names beside the mapping (decision mimid-1wgh.143), and the persisted history is bead mimid-1wgh.140.8.
